questions.q: What does the `FROM` instruction do in a Dockerfile?
options: It specifies the final command the container runs
It sets the base image that the rest of the Dockerfile builds on top of
It copies files from the host into the image
It names the resulting image
questions.explain: FROM sets the starting point -- an existing image (like node:20-slim) that every following instruction builds on top of.

questions.q: In the Northbridge Dockerfile, why is `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` followed by `RUN npm install` before the later `COPY . .`?
options: Dockerfiles require all COPY instructions to list specific filenames before any wildcard copy
It copies just the dependency manifests and installs them first, before bringing in the rest of the application code -- which matters for build speed, covered in the next lesson
It has no effect either way; the order is purely stylistic
node:20-slim requires package.json to be copied before WORKDIR is set
questions.explain: Splitting dependency installation from the rest of the code copy is deliberate, setting up the layer-caching behavior covered in Lesson 12 -- code changes shouldn't force a full dependency reinstall.

questions.q: What does `EXPOSE 3000` in a Dockerfile actually do?
options: It automatically publishes port 3000 on the host when the container runs
It documents that the container listens on port 3000, but does not by itself publish anything -- you still need -p or -P on docker run
It opens port 3000 for traffic only from other containers, never from the host
It sets the container's internal clock to port 3000's time zone
questions.explain: EXPOSE is informational documentation inside the image. Actually publishing the port to the host still requires -p or -P when running the container, as covered in Lesson 8.

questions.q: In `docker build -t northbridge/catalog:1.4 .`, what is the trailing `.`?
options: A typo that Docker ignores
The build context -- the directory Docker reads the Dockerfile and COPY sources from
The version number of the image
A flag that enables verbose build logging
questions.explain: The final argument to docker build is the build context: the directory whose files are available to COPY/ADD instructions and where Docker looks for the Dockerfile by default.

questions.q: What does `CMD ["node", "server.js"]` specify in a Dockerfile?
options: The name the image will be tagged with
The default command a container runs when it's started from this image
A command that only runs during the build, not when the container starts
The port the container will listen on
questions.explain: CMD sets the default command executed when a container is started from the image -- here, launching the Node server.
